takeaway: More of the same rainy-season rhythm for now: hot, mostly sunny mornings, then afternoon storms, with a chance of early-morning showers along the coast as a tropical wave passes Friday. The bigger news is the wind. The marine forecast now shows the Caribbean trade winds arriving Sunday, turning northeast to east by Sunday night, which is offshore for Nosara. All the models agree those trades hold for most of next week, which should mean cleaner surf mornings and a drier Pacific side. A long-period south-southwest swell is already running. No storms threaten Costa Rica. Multi-day soaking rain stays watch-only, and slightly less likely than yesterday.

periods.label: Days 1–3 (Wed–Fri, Oct 7–9)
periods.pattern: Local heating runs the show. Costa Rica's weather service expects a partly cloudy, very warm morning (Nicoya near 34–35°C), then scattered showers and thunderstorms in the afternoon, with Guanacaste among the most active areas. A few showers can linger into the night, and there's a chance of coastal showers on the peninsula overnight and at first light. A tropical wave passes Friday, which raises the odds of early-day rain along the coast Thursday into the weekend. Model averages show light to moderate daily rain over the peninsula, heavier in the mountains.
periods.implications: Mornings are the best window for anything outdoors, but don't be surprised by a pre-dawn or early shower Thursday or Friday. Plan around afternoon storms with lightning.
periods.confidence: High on sunny-morning, stormy-afternoon days. Moderate on exactly when cells hit Nosara.

periods.label: Days 4–7 (Sat–Tue, Oct 10–13)
periods.pattern: The weekend is the hand-off. Saturday still looks like a typical rainy-season day after the tropical wave. From Sunday the Caribbean trade winds push across Nicaragua and northern Costa Rica and out over the Gulf of Papagayo, and every model shows them strengthening Monday and Tuesday. The rain averages put the heaviest rain just offshore Sunday and Monday, then it starts shifting away from our coast by Tuesday. The U.S. hurricane center expects a low to form south of Guatemala early next week, heading away to the west-northwest.
periods.implications: Keep Saturday flexible. Sunday through Tuesday should trend toward cleaner mornings and fewer storms on our side, although a stormy afternoon or two is still likely early on.
periods.confidence: Moderate to high that the trades return Sunday or Monday. Moderate on how fast the rain eases.

periods.label: Days 8–15 (Wed–Wed, Oct 14–21)
periods.pattern: Most guidance now favors a trade-wind week. The European AI and standard European ensembles keep steady easterly winds over Nicaragua and Costa Rica through about Oct 19, with lighter rain on our Pacific side and the heavier rain on the Caribbean coast. The U.S. ensemble also builds the trades but keeps more rain just off the Pacific coast around Oct 13–16 before easing. Several models show a low well offshore south of Guatemala or El Salvador around Oct 17–19, far enough away that it mainly matters for wind and swell, not rain here. Costa Rica's long-range outlook still calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25, no extreme events, and very dry weather from about Oct 26.
periods.implications: This leans toward a drier, sunnier stretch with fewer afternoon storms than usual for October. It's a reasonable week for rain-sensitive plans, with the Oct 13–16 period the least certain.
periods.confidence: Moderate. Better agreement than yesterday, but the U.S. model still holds out for a wetter few days.

surfWinds.regime: Light and variable through Saturday (northwest to north at times), then Caribbean trades (offshore at Nosara) arriving Sunday and holding into next week.
surfWinds.detail: The Papagayo marine forecast (issued 3:10 a.m. PDT Wednesday) has variable winds under 5 knots today, going northwest around 10 knots late tonight. Thursday through Saturday it's north to northwest around 10 knots, mostly at night and in the morning, with calmer spells in between. Northwest is side-onshore at Nosara, while north is closer to cross-shore. Light and variable does not mean glassy offshore. It just means no trade wind, so the sea breeze still takes over by late morning. Sunday turns north-northeast 10–15 knots, then northeast to east 10–15 knots Sunday night. That's the real Caribbean trade, which is offshore for Nosara. Seas are 3–5 feet today in a south-southwest swell with long 18-second periods, then 4–6 feet through the weekend as the period eases to about 13–15 seconds. Nicaragua: the models show the trades blowing across Nicaragua and out over the Pacific from Sunday, strengthening Monday and Tuesday, and staying fairly steady through about Oct 19. All-day offshore in Nicaragua would be a good sign for strong, clean Nosara mornings, but it doesn't guarantee all-day offshore here. Expect the sea breeze to fight back some afternoons.
surfWinds.bestWindows: Through Saturday, dawn patrol before the sea breeze or the northwest wind fills in, and the long-period swell is worth getting up for. From Sunday, and especially Monday Oct 12 onward, expect the best offshore morning glass of the month so far, possibly holding later into the day when the trades are strong.
surfWinds.confidence: High on light winds through Saturday. Moderate to high on the trades arriving Sunday or Monday. Moderate on how long they hold past Oct 17.

gyreWatch.status: Watch only, nothing established. Slightly lower than yesterday.
gyreWatch.possibleTiming: Oct 13–16 is the only window with a wet signal, mostly from the U.S. ensemble, and mainly just offshore.
gyreWatch.supporting: The U.S. ensemble keeps heavier rain just off the Pacific coast Oct 13–16 and shows southwest winds pushing toward southern Costa Rica around Oct 15. The hurricane center gives a low south of Guatemala a 30% chance of developing in the next week (up from 20%). The U.S. tropics outlook updated Oct 6 sees another possible system south of Mexico in the week of Oct 14–20.
gyreWatch.conflicting: Every model family now builds firm Caribbean trades from about Oct 11–12, which normally means a drier Pacific side, not a multi-day soaking. Both European ensembles keep our side fairly dry and push the heavy rain to the Caribbean coast. The lows the models show stay well offshore to the northwest and move away. Costa Rica's long-range outlook calls for less rain than normal Oct 12–25 with no extreme events, and the new U.S. tropics outlook dropped last week's mention of a possible Central American gyre.

whatChanged: The official marine forecast now shows northeast to east trade winds arriving Sunday night. Yesterday it had northwest to north wind through Saturday and nothing beyond. All the models still bring the trades back around Oct 11–13, and the European ensembles now hold them through about Oct 19. The swell is now running with longer 18-second periods today. The hurricane center raised the chance of the low south of Guatemala to 30% (from 20%). The U.S. tropics outlook updated and no longer mentions a Central American gyre. Its main local note is below-normal rain over the Caribbean region. The U.S. ensemble is still the wet outlier for Oct 13–16, but its wet area is now mostly offshore. Prolonged-rain risk is a touch lower. Costa Rica's weather service hasn't issued a new alert today; yesterday's said hot, humid mornings would set up afternoon downpours.
practical: Get outside in the morning and plan around afternoon storms through Saturday, with a possible early shower Thursday or Friday from the tropical wave. Surf dawn patrol now for the long-period swell. Circle Sunday to Tuesday (Oct 11–13) for the return of offshore trades and cleaner mornings, likely lasting much of next week. Next week looks drier than normal on our side. No tropical storm threat to Costa Rica.
